div.head: Wer 5
div.ab: Healsfang gebyreð bearnum, broðrum ⁊ fæderan; ne gebyreð nanum mæge ðæt feoð bute ðam ðe sy binnan cneowe.
Healsfang gebyreð bearnum, broðrum ⁊ fæderan; ne gebyreð nanum mæge þæt feoh bute ðam ðe sy binnam cweowe.
Healsfangum debent habere filii, fratres et federan (id est fratres patris); non pertinet alii cognationi pecunia ista nisi illis qui sunt intra cneoƿe (id est genu).
‘Halsfang’ gebührt [des Erschlagenen] Kindern, Brüdern und Vatersbruder [-brüdern?]; dies Geld gebührt keinem Verwandten, ausser dem, der innerhalb des Knies steht.
The healsfang belongs to [the slain man's] children, brothers and father's brother [brothers?]; this money belongs to no kinsman except one who stands within the knee [degree].
Healsfang is due to the children, brothers and fathers; that money is not due to any to any kin except those within the knee.
div.note: U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; B reads ‘binnam cweowe’ (so); Liebermann would correct to ‘cneowe’. H reads ‘feoð’, to be corrected to ‘feoh’.

note.seg: Dieser Satz scheint mir den Zusammenhang des die Totschlagsühne regelnden Stückes zu unterbrechen, daher wie 3¹. 4¹ späterer Zusatz. Phillpotts (Kindred 243 die ‘within the first knee’ missversteht) hält ‘Vatersbruder’ für den Irrtum eines Dänen: grundlos

This sentence seems to me to interrupt the continuity of the piece regulating the settlement of homicide, and is therefore, like 3¹. 4¹, a later addition. Phillpotts (Kindred 243, who misunderstands ‘within the first knee’) regards ‘father’s brother’ as the error of a Dane: without grounds

Auch wenn fæderan den Sing. bedeutet—was nicht sicher, da die Schreiber HB um 1120 -an statt -um gesetzt haben können—, so meint er doch alle Verwandte dieses Grades, also Plural, wie Q versteht.—Nicht für Mutterrechtspur ist dies anzuführen, da kein Mutterbruder erwähnt wird

Even if fæderan means the sing. — which is not certain, since the scribes of HB c. 1120 may have put -an for -um —, it nevertheless means all relatives of this degree, i.e. a plural, as Q understands it. — This is not to be cited as a trace of mother-right, since no mother’s brother is mentioned
